messages:
Priya: FYI customer AcmeGames reporting repeated 429s during peak gameplay spikes. They say bursts used to be fine but started failing yesterday afternoon.
Mike: ok can you paste the error payload and a short repro? 429 usually means burst credits exhausted or a hard quota hit.
Priya: pasted below from the customer's logs — they get "error": {"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"burst credits exhausted"} and SDK retries end up backoff-ing. They reported ~2–3s windows of 120 req/s on top of a steady 10 req/s.
Jordan: that sounds like short sharp spikes. Are they on default smoothing?
Priya: yes default. They expected burst credits to cover that pattern. They sent a histogram: avg baseline 10 rps, spike to 120 rps for 2–5s, repeats every ~30s for a few mins.
rate-limit-bot: [automated] quota-check: account=acme-games tier=standard burst_credits_remaining=0 hard_quota_used=45%
Lina: any recent config changes to their project? token rotation? model changes?
Priya: no changes on their side. No model switch. SDK version 2.4.1.
Mike: two likely causes: 1) spike pattern is faster than the burst refill rate so credits deplete; 2) they may have concurrent endpoints consuming same bucket. We need to confirm bucket footprint.
Priya: requested sample request IDs and time windows — sending a snippet from the app: ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Body: {"model":"redwood-13b","input":"..."}
```
They show back-to-back calls from many worker processes.
Jordan: can we reproduce locally with a simple load script to confirm burst credit behaviour? I can run a quick k6 across 100 connections to simulate 120 rps bursts.
Mike: please do. Also grab the `x-rate-limit` headers from the failing responses — `x-rate-limit-burst-remaining` and `x-rate-limit-reset` if present. That will confirm whether this is burst bucket exhaustion vs global throttle.
Priya: customer attached these headers for a failing request: `x-rate-limit-burst-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-window: 60`, `x-rate-limit-replenish-rate: 2` (approx).
Lina: replenish-rate=2 tokens/sec with a window=60 implies bursts refill slowly. If spike is 120 rps for several seconds, credits gone quickly.
Mike: matches. Two mitigation routes: short-term smoothing policy (limit their max burst concurrency to ~20–30rps smoothing) OR temporarily bump their burst bucket/limit while we investigate usage pattern + recommend client-side token bucket smoothing on their side.
Priya: customer wants immediate fix — they have live players. What's the quickest safe action?
Mike: we can apply a transient smoothing policy at the edge to damp spikes: `smoothing.max_burst=30, smoothing.window=5s` which will allow short bursts but cap the instantaneous rate. That avoids exhausting credits while preserving baseline. It'll also buy time for engineering to tune refill.
Jordan: I can apply that policy and monitor. How long should we leave it? 24–72h?
Mike: start with 6 hours, monitor errors. If stable, extend to 24h and open a follow-up to determine longer-term quota change or client-side fixes.
Priya: I'm going to ask billing if we can temporarily allocate more burst credits or bump their tier until this is sorted. @Billing any quick options?
Billing: can do a short-term uplift of burst allowance for emergency incidents. Need account id + approver. I'll standby for those.
Priya: Account: acct_01AG55. Approver: VP of Ops at Acme (email in ticket). They approved a temporary uplift for 48h.
rate-limit-bot: [automated] policy-change: smoothing applied account=acct_01AG55 smoothing.max_burst=30 smoothing.window=5s (applied by Jordan)
Priya: applied and customer reports immediate drop in 429s. They see slightly increased latency for some requests but overall stable.
Mike: good. Next steps: 1) eng-runtime to look at refill rates and whether the replenish-rate calculation needs to consider short-window telemetry; 2) recommend client changes: jittered token bucket, backoff retries with `Retry-After`, decrease concurrency; 3) billing to confirm 48h uplift completed in backend.
Lina: for the engineering ticket include: sample traffic traces, `x-rate-limit-*` headers, spike histogram, and which endpoints consumed the most tokens (embedding vs text-generation).
Priya: created internal ticket INF-8421 and attached customer traces and headers.
Billing: uplift applied in billing UI and flagged on the invoice. Confirmed 48h starting now.
Mike: I'll run the k6 spike test and post results. If runtime needs to tweak kernel-level refill calc, tag eng-runtime and we'll prioritize.
Jordan: k6 run shows the following (summarized): baseline preserved, initial burst capped by smoothing, 429s dropped from ~30% to ~1% during repeated spike cycles. Posting raw output in thread.
Priya: Customer verified on their side as well — "we see stable gameplay now, thank you" :thumbsup:
Lina: add a short-note to the docs about recommended smoothing for gaming-style 2–5s microbursts. Could help other customers.
Mike: Agreed. I'll open a docs PR with config snippets and sample rates.
Priya: closing loop with customer and confirming we'll follow up after uplift expires to either extend or implement permanent quota change.
Jordan: follow-up scheduled in 2 days to reassess.
Priya: thanks all, logging resolution in the support ticket.
